lines.text: Do you know how a busy kitchen gets your order right? It runs on little slips called tickets.
When you order, the server sends it to the kitchen, and it splits up. The grill gets your burger. The fry station gets your chips.
Each cook only sees their part, so nobody wastes time reading the whole order.
Many kitchens use screens now. Each ticket shows a timer, and turns yellow, then red, if it waits too long.
At the pass, one person called the expo checks every plate, and only sends the order out when it's all there.
The idea goes back to the eighteen hundreds, when chef Auguste Escoffier organised kitchens like an army, with a station for everything.
Orbi Work runs on the same idea. Type a task, tag a teammate, and it moves step by step. Doing, review, done. And everyone sees it live.
